business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Portable Phased-Array Medical Diagnostic Scanners

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid / Bijural: Private law and partnerships governed by Civil Law (Civil Code of Quebec, CQLR c CCQ-1991); public, federal commercial, and regulatory matters governed by Common Law and federal statutes (PCBMLTFA, etc.); public law in Quebec follows the civil-law legislative model but procedural rules are hybrid.

Canada-China Tax Agreement (Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation), S.C. 1986, c. 48, in force 29 Dec 1986
Canada-Hong Kong Agreement for the Avoidance of Double Taxation, in force 1 Oct 2013
Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA/USMCA), in force 1 Jul 2020 (medical-device tariff-free trade)
Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) between Canada and the EU, provisionally in force 21 Sep 2017

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), S.C. 2000, c.17; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c.C-46, ss.83.01-83.33; Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c.17; United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c.U-2; Canada Business Corporations Act (public UBO register regime, where applicable). Provincial: Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1 and Regulation CQLR c P-44.1, r.1 (UBO declarations and REQ register); Civil Code of Quebec, arts.2236-2266 (société en commandite / limited partnership); Act to enhance the transparency of enterprises, L.Q. 2021, c.19; Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11. Sectoral: Food and Drugs Act, R.S.C. 1985, c.F-27; Medical Devices Regulations, SOR/98-282.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (PRC MFA/FAO) + OCCQ certified French translation; consular legalization no longer required under the Apostille Convention

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-acceptance screening of all general partners, limited partners beneficial owners, directors, and authorized signatories against: (i) Canada's consolidated sanctions lists under SEMA and the United Nations Act (Global Affairs Canada); (ii) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) OFAC SDN List and 50% Rule (for USD-denominated Swift LC and TT wire rails); (iv) UK HMT and EU lists where counterparties are EU/UK-linked; (v) FINTRAC indicators for politically exposed persons (domestic and foreign PEPs, heads of international organizations, their family members and close associates per PCMLTFA s.9.3-9.4 and FINTRAC guidance). Screening is to be re-run at onboarding, at each capital call/contribution, and at least monthly thereafter; results logged and retained for a minimum of 5 years (7 years recommended under PCMLTFA). Direct or indirect exposure to designated or sanctioned persons bars the LP from formation and triggers a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) to FINTRAC where a transaction has already occurred.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - online name search and reservation service (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca / Registre des entreprises: Centre de recherche et de réservation des noms)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11) and the Regulation respecting the language of commerce and business, the business name must be in French. A transliteration (romanization) of a foreign name may be used if combined with a French expression, but the French form must be complete and prevail. Latin characters with standard French accents are required; non-Latin scripts (e.g., Chinese characters) are not permitted in the registered name but may appear as a secondary trademark, provided the French name is prominently displayed on products, signage and commercial contracts in Quebec. Pinyin transliteration must respect French phonetics where possible; English-only names are rejected unless recognized exceptions apply.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Trust / Fiducie (reserved for regulated trust companies)
Avocat / Lawyer / Barreau (reserved for members of the Barreau du Québec)
Notaire / Notary (reserved for notaries of the Chambre des notaires du Québec)
Médecin / Doctor / Clinic - where implying medical practice
Ingénieur / Engineer (reserved for OIQ-licensed engineers in professional context)
Régie / Commission / Bureau / Ministère / Gouvernement / Canada / Québec / Municipal (words that falsely suggest a government authority or public body)
Université / Collège / École (reserved for licensed educational institutions)
Corporation / Incorporate / Inc. / Ltée / SARL / LLP / LP - only in a fashion consistent with the actual legal form (for an LP: 'société en commandite', 'S.E.C.' or 'L.P.' permitted suffixes)
Terms contrary to public order, morality, or likely to mislead third parties as to the nature of the enterprise (Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, s.16-18)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the REQ rejects or objects to a proposed name, the applicant may file a written request for review (demande de révision) with the Registraire within 30 days of the notice of refusal, setting out submissions on distinctiveness and compliance with the French-language rules. A further judicial review (révision judiciaire) may be sought before the Cour du Québec (civil division) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. In parallel, the applicant may file an amended declaration with a new proposed name, or request a 90-day extension of a reservation prior to its expiry (renewal available upon payment of the applicable fee). Legal counsel should first obtain a 'NEGATIVE' clearance response in writing and then either: (i) add a distinctive French element (e.g., 'AxonVision Ultrason Médical S.E.C.'), or (ii) appeal per s.11 of the Act and the rules of administrative procedure of the REQ.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted subject to conditions: the registered office (siège social) of the société en commandite must be a real, physical address in Quebec where documents may be served, and the REQ requires a civic address (no P.O. Box only). A licensed 'domiciliation' service (centres de domiciliation) providing a physical street address in Quebec, mail forwarding, and acceptance of service is accepted by the REQ for a limited partnership, provided the service contract explicitly designates the domiciliary service provider as authorized to receive service of process during registration hours. A pure virtual office without service acceptance is not compliant. For a medical device manufacturer, the REQ address cannot be a mere virtual office in isolation; a physical manufacturing/QC site in Quebec (leased or owned) is expected to support Health Canada MDEL pre-inspection and ISO 13485 audits.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-high (estimated 65-80% probability within the first 18 months of operation): Health Canada may conduct a Good Manufacturing Practices inspection (under the Medical Devices Regulations and ISO 13485) before or shortly after granting the Medical Device Establishment Licence; the Régie du bâtiment / local fire and municipal authorities may inspect commercial premises; REQ may verify the registered office through service-of-process checks. For an L.P. exporting diagnostic ultrasound consoles, Health Canada reserves the right to conduct unannounced post-market surveillance inspections and customs audits, particularly where the manufacturing site is newly established and foreign-owned.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec, CQLR c CCQ, arts. 2232–2266 (limited partnership), and Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, ss. 2, 15–17 (registration and public disclosure)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation d'une société en commandite (Declaration of Registration of a Limited Partnership)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a limited partnership. The declaration and partnership agreement must state the agreed contributions of the partners; limited partners may not act for or bind the partnership. No escrow account is required. The general partner remains fully and unconditionally liable for partnership obligations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) the General Partner approves the formation of the limited partnership and subscribes to the general-partner interest in the amount stated in the partnership agreement; (2) subscriptions from prospective limited partners are accepted, with capital contributions to be credited to the partnership accounts as agreed; (3) the registered office is established at [registered office address in Quebec, Canada], and the Registraire des entreprises du Québec is instructed to file the Declaration of Registration; (4) [Designated officer/manager] is appointed as authorized signatory of the partnership, empowered to open bank accounts, execute leases, apply for all government permits, and appoint tax preparers; (5) all actions necessary to complete statutory formation and federal, provincial, and regulatory filings are ratified and approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search and Lodging of Partnership Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – Online Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search using the REQ's online enterprise register. Prepare the Déclaration d'immatriculation de société en commandite, including the proposed partnership name, registered office address, objects, term, identity, and address of every general partner and limited partner, and specify the amount and nature of each partner's contribution. Sign the declaration and retain the signed version for filing.
required_dossiers: Name search report from the Quebec enterprise register
Draft limited partnership agreement
Proof of identity and address for all partners
Registered office address in Quebec
Declaration form signed by all general partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ issues a prior-approval query concerning the proposed name, submit a corrected declaration eliminating the conflict or file a written consent/waiver from the prior name holder. Corrections are accepted online without reopening the entire application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Declaration of Registration with REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – Filing and Publicity Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online registration through REQ's declaration deposit service, upload the signed declaration, pay the applicable filing fee by credit card or electronic transfer, and download the acknowledgement and provisional NEQ number issued by the REQ immediately upon successful filing.
required_dossiers: Completed and signed Declaration of Registration
Power of attorney and notarized signature if submitted by an agent
Proof of payment of the registration fee
Supporting document evidencing the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ rejects or queries the declaration, the registrant receives a notice of refusal. Cure the irregularity by filing an amended declaration through the REQ portal, or contest the refusal before the Court of Québec within the statutory review period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Creation of Federal Business Number and Provincial Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online; Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the NEQ issued by the REQ, register the limited partnership with the CRA for a federal Business Number and GST/HST, payroll, and income-tax program accounts. Then register through Revenu Québec for Quebec sales tax (QST), source deductions, and employer accounts, linking all provincial registrations to the NEQ.
required_dossiers: NEQ confirmation notice
Declaration of Registration receipt
Authorized officer identification
Banking details for tax account refunds and direct deposits
Contact details of the partnership's Quebec registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA or Revenu Québec identifies a discrepancy between the NEC and filed federal/provincial programs, correct the registration through the respective online authentication portal or call the CRA's business enquiries line using the REQ file number to reconcile the records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Governance Documents and Partnership Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internal Governance – Legal Counsel and Corporate Secretary in Quebec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the formal limited partnership agreement, issue capital-contribution statements to each partner, establish the partnership minute book, and maintain a register of partners at the registered office. Record the pro-forma first board resolution in the minute book and have the general partner execute banking resolutions.
required_dossiers: Final limited partnership agreement
Capital contribution receipts from all partners
Register of partners and managers
Minute book with pro-forma first board resolution
Consent of the general partner to legal representation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a partner disputes the recorded contributions, issue an amended capital statement and obtain a written consent from the affected partner. Any material change to the partnership agreement must be reflected in an amended declaration filed with the REQ.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration for Workplace Safety, Payroll and Employer Obligations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST); Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Quebec establishment with the CNESST for occupational health and safety coverage, open the employer payroll account, and register for CNESST contribution payments. Submit the notice of opening of a workplace if the industrial establishment involves manufacturing operations, and follow the prescribed posting and health-and-safety obligations.
required_dossiers: QST and source deduction account numbers
Employer declaration with CNESST
Establishment activity code (NAICS 334510 or 3250)
List of initial employees and hire dates
Description of the workplace physical facilities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CNESST reclassifies the establishment activity code from the submitted manufacturing category, request a reclassification review through the CNESST online services and provide a detailed production and operation description supporting the requested code.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Medical Device Establishment Licence Application with Health Canada
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Health Canada – Medical Devices Directorate, e-Submission Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a Medical Device Establishment Licence (MDEL) application for the manufacturing and importation of the color Doppler ultrasound console, supported by the ISO 13485 quality management system certificate and device classification under the applicable risk class. Address the requirements of Part 2 of the Medical Devices Regulations (SOR/98-282), including objective evidence of the quality system and traceability procedures.
required_dossiers: MDEL application form completed in English or French
ISO 13485 certificate or equivalent quality system documentation
Risk classification determination for the color Doppler ultrasound console
Site facilities description and process flow
Product labelling and instructions for use draft for regulatory conformity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Health Canada sends a deficiency letter within 30 days of receipt, respond with the required supporting documentation within the indicated timeline, normally 60 days. If the MDEL is refused, submit a revised application or a section 40 prior-approval application with expert justification for the device's safety and effectiveness.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Medical Device Establishment Licence (MDEL) under the Food and Drugs Act, RSC 1985, c F-27, and the Medical Devices Regulations, SOR/98-282, s. 44

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Medical device assembly and low-emissions manufacturing is generally outside the mandatory full EIA schedule; the project is subject to the prior authorization and declaration regime under section 22 of the Environment Quality Act (CQLR c E-1, s. 22). A full EIA report is not required unless the facility uses hazardous solvents or chemicals listed in the applicable environmental assessment schedules.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must meet municipal sewer by-law limits and provincial effluent quality criteria for protection of aquatic life, including suspended solids and metals. Volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions are subject to the Règlement sur l'assainissement de l'air, CQLR c Q-2, r. 1.1, requiring best available control technology, localized concentration limits, and closed-loop solvent handling where applicable. Hazardous waste must be transported and traced through authorized carriers under the Règlement sur les matières dangereuses.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: obtain a fire inspection certificate from the competent local fire safety service for the industrial occupancy before beginning operation. Structural load inspections: retain an engineer to certify mezzanine and equipment loads at the manufacturing site. Occupational clearance: file a notice of opening with the CNESST and obtain a workplace compliance certificate covering machine guarding, electrical safety, noise, optical radiation (ultrasound and display screens), and walkway clearances.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — for federal GST/HST and income tax; Revenu Québec (Revenue Quebec) for Quebec Sales Tax (QST), Quebec income tax, and payroll-related levies. Portals: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html) and Revenu Québec CLIC online services (https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — Register the Limited Partnership in Quebec by filing a declaration of registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) to obtain the Numéro d'entreprise du Québec (NEQ), a prerequisite for QST registration. Step 2 — Obtain the federal Business Number (BN) from the CRA through Business Registration Online (BRO) or by filing Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number); non-resident applicants may use CRA's International Tax Services Office (+1-800-959-5525; outside North America +1-613-940-9247). Step 3 — Activate the GST/HST program account (BN-RT0001) for the partnership's commercial activity. Step 4 — Register separately for QST with Revenu Québec by filing Form LM-1-V or via CLIC using the NEQ and CRA registration data. Step 5 — Complete registration within 30 days after the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold is exceeded; non-resident partners must designate a Canadian representative (Form RC59) and may be required to post security under Excise Tax Act s. 240(2). Supporting due diligence: certified partnership agreement, foreign registration certificate, and notarized powers of attorney.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible. The Quebec LP is fiscally transparent for federal and Quebec income tax: the LP files an information-only T5013 (and Quebec equivalent) and does not pay income tax at the entity level; each partner, including non-resident partners, is liable on the allocated share of Canadian-source business income. For GST/HST and QST, the Excise Tax Act and the Quebec Taxation Act treat the partnership as a separate person, so the LP must maintain its own GST/HST and QST registrations and remit net tax in the partnership's name. A non-resident partner's Canadian tax exposure is limited to income attributable to the LP's Quebec carrying-on-business, subject to treaty sourcing rules; the LP remains an entity-level registrant for indirect taxes and a withholding vehicle for payments to non-resident partners.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box entity classification election; pass-through is the statutory default for eligible LPs. Relevant elections: (i) a joint election under Article IV(7) of the Canada-US Tax Convention allows the LP and its US-resident partners to treat the LP as a corporation solely for treaty benefits (filing accompanies the T5013 or the partners' returns); (ii) Income Tax Act s. 96(3) joint election to be recognized as a Canadian partnership when all partners are Canadian residents, enabling tax-deferred transfers; (iii) for GST/QST, the quick method of accounting (Form GST74) and quarterly or annual filing elections are available to qualifying registrants; (iv) hybrid mismatch rules in ITA ss. 18.4–18.6 apply de jure and are not elective, denying deductions on hybrid instruments and disregarded payments between Canadian and foreign related entities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST and QST — the federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) at 5% and the Quebec Sales Tax (QST) at 9.975%, with QST computed on the GST-inclusive selling price in Quebec, producing an effective combined burden of approximately 15.47% on the pre-tax price; Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) does not apply in Quebec. Both are value-added taxes with input-tax-credit (ITC) and input-tax-refund (ITR) recovery, administered respectively by the CRA and Revenu Québec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — the small-supplier threshold is reached when worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 over any four consecutive calendar quarters, or in the current calendar quarter where the person has no prior business. Once exceeded, GST/HST registration is mandatory within 30 days (ETA s. 240); the parallel QST registration threshold before Revenu Québec is also CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies. Registrants making exclusively zero-rated exports must nevertheless register to recover input tax credits on export-related purchases.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Quebec do not impose real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or a mandatory B2B e-invoicing API. GST/HST remittances are filed via CRA GST/HST NETFILE (or Form GST34); Revenu Québec requires electronic transmission of QST remittances for registrants above its filing thresholds. Voluntary e-invoicing follows the Pan-Canadian PEPPOL BIS 3.0 standard, which is mandatory for suppliers billing the federal government through PSPC where the contract requires e-invoicing. Invoices must be retained for six years in a readable format and must display the prescribed text 'GST/HST included at 5%' and 'QST included at 9.975%' where applicable; no government pre-approval or stamping regime exists.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods are zero-rated under ETA Schedule VI, Part V, item 1 provided the registrant supplier, as part of the supply, ships the goods to a destination outside Canada: goods must be delivered to a common carrier for export or exported by the supplier within the statutory time window (generally 60 days after the supply, unless the Minister allows a longer period), and the exporter must retain evidence meeting the Exporters of Records Regulations (SOR/99-164). Supplies of services to non-residents are zero-rated under Part V, item 23 unless the service relates to real or tangible personal property in Canada or is a personal service; installation and training performed in Canada on the ultrasound console are taxable and should be separately invoiced. The reciprocal QST zero-rating under the Quebec Taxation Act mirrors these rules. The recipient must be a non-resident and the goods must not be acquired for consumption or use in Canada; a B13A export declaration processed through the CBSA's Canadian Export Reporting System substantiates the export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A filed via the Canadian Export Reporting System (CESR); mandatory for shipments exceeding CAD 2,000, with a low-value shipment exemption below that amount)
Commercial Invoice (full description, HS tariff classification 9018.12 or 9018.13 for ultrasound devices, unit value, currency, terms of sale, destination, and consignee identity)
Bill of Lading (ocean) or Air Waybill (air) naming the Canadian exporter and the foreign consignee, evidencing outbound movement
ACI eManifest confirmation (Advance Commercial Information transmitted by the carrier to the CBSA before departure)
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank SWIFT MT103 or TT credit advice evidencing that export proceeds have been or will be repatriated within the 180-day compliance window)
Health Canada Medical Device Establishment Licence and Export Certificate under the Medical Devices Regulations (SOR/98-282), where applicable for the destination market
Packing list, calculation-of-origin statement, and certificate of origin (e.g., CETA, CPTPP, USMCA) where an FTA preference is claimed
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess within the four-year normal reassessment period for GST/QST (three or four years for income tax depending on partner status), with no time limit where misrepresentation or fraud is shown (ETA s. 298; ITA s. 152(4)). Denial of export zero-rating — due to late exportation, defective bills of lading, shell foreign consignees, or unsubstantiated inward remittances — triggers assessment of the full GST (5%) and QST (9.975%) on the invoice value plus prescribed compound interest. Penalties include: ETA s. 285 gross-negligence penalty (greater of CAD 250 and 25% of net tax avoided); ETA s. 280 failure-to-register penalty; late-filing and late-remittance penalties (1% of the balance plus 0.25% per month, maximum 12 months); CBSA AMPS monetary penalties up to CAD 25,000 per export misdeclaration; and criminal prosecution under ETA s. 327 or ITA s. 239 with fines up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to five years. CRA export-task-force audits of medical-device exporters routinely require the full documentation bundle to be produced within 30 days of request.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) and the Department of Finance administer related oversight, but Canada maintains no specialized foreign-exchange control authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada applies full convertibility on both current and capital account transactions. There are no exchange controls requiring central bank approval, no CAD repatriation limits, and no restriction on paying dividends, partnership distributions, or export proceeds to non-residents, provided (i) the partnership is in good standing under provincial and federal laws, (ii) withholding requirements under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (Canada) or Part I (Quebec) are addressed, and (iii) payments are not blocked by sanctions or U.S. dollar clearing-house restrictions. The medium- to long-term funding position of the LP should nevertheless be aligned with transfer-pricing and thin-capitalization rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender obligation or mandatory conversion ratio applies under Canadian federal or Quebec law. Exporters and manufacturers may retain invoices in foreign currency and operate foreign-currency bank accounts. All exports of medical devices must nevertheless be reported for customs/statistics under the Customs Act and the Export and Import Permits Act; the exporter should declare the transaction to the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) if required. Where proceeds are received, FINTRAC large-cash transaction reporting thresholds apply to receipts of CAD 10,000 or more and to cross-border wire transfers, but no repatriation deadline exists.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Canada does not regulate EMIs as a separate category; non-bank fintechs require money-services business (MSB) or foreign-money-services business (FMSB) registration with FINTRAC when carrying out any transfer/payment activity on behalf of the LP. Offshore digital EMIs are generally not acceptable conduits for the structural capital escrow or for regulatory-required commercial settlements; their viability is Medium as a secondary collection/payment initiation channel only where the EMI is FINTRAC-registered or holds a Quebec/Canadian money-services license, and Low where it relies solely on a foreign e-money authorization without a Canadian nexus.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No blanket statutory requirement exists that directors appear physically before the bank in Quebec; the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) permits non-face-to-face account opening where the bank applies enhanced identity verification using dual-source independent confirmation, corporate registry searches, and electronic authentication. In practice, major Canadian banks may request at least one authorized signatory or a place-of-business visit for non-resident and partnership accounts, especially when the partnership has no established credit history. For a Quebec LP, completion of the Quebec enterprise register's Registraire des entreprises extract and up-to-date provincial authorization is mandatory before any account application.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident general partner or limited partners with opaque ownership layers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full partnership agreement, register of partners, Canadian-recorded declarations, CRS/FATCA tax-residency self-certification forms, and a beneficial ownership attestation demonstrating the ultimate natural persons below Canada's 25% threshold.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Limited partnership structure with no minimum capital requirement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Evidence of initial capital contribution, inwards wire or bankers draft, sourceof-funds documentation, capital commitment schedule, and a cash-flow projection consistent with the proposed medical-device export activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border medical device export activity flagged as dual-use or high-value
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Health Canada medical device establishment licence or applicable export permit, distribution contracts, pro-forma invoices, ISO 13485 certification, and the US FDA or EU CE marking evidence where relevant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of Canadian physical substance or registered office concerns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Canadian lease agreement, proof of payroll filings with Revenu Québec and the CRA, the LP's Quebec enterprise number registration, a registered place of business, and notarized confirmation of the local registered agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual funding through offshore intermediate holding vehicles
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-wealth report for each material funder, audited financial statements of the intermediate entity, notarized statutory declarations, organizational chart evidencing economic rationale, and copies of subscription agreements or loan contracts.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Incoming equity/debt contributions should be remitted via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 for CAD clearing, using the bank's correspondent arrangement through Lynx (Canada's high-value payment system). Recommended wire instructions include the LP's Canadian bank account, full legal name, Quebec enterprise number, and purpose narrative 'Capital contribution to limited partnership' or 'Foreign direct investment - equity participation'. The remitter must ensure originator information conforms to FINTRAC wire-transfer rules; the bank will verify source of funds and may request the partnership agreement and capital commitment schedule. For amounts exceeding CAD 10,000, FINTRAC large-cash transaction reporting and electronic funds transfer reports may apply.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements, preferred rails are (i) direct SWIFT MT103 for T/T payments in USD/CAD/EUR, and (ii) commercial letters of credit issued or applicable under UCP600 for the sale of color Doppler ultrasound consoles. The bank will clear CAD domestically through Lynx and cross-border in USD through its U.S. correspondent (CHIPS/Fedwire). Documentary compliance must include commercial invoice, bill of lading, packing list, certificate of origin, and medical device export compliance evidence. The LP may maintain segregated foreign-currency accounts for disbursement and remittance paperwork.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Delivery-based FX forwards with maturity up to 12 months subject to bank ISDA/CSA documentation
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for genuinely restricted settlement currencies and not for CAD/USD/EUR
Cross-currency swaps for long-term matched funding of equipment sales or leases
Plain-vanilla forward-exchange contracts offered by Schedule I Canadian banks

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each annual registration anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fees applied by the registrar; failure to file for two consecutive years permits administrative dissolution/strike-off of the registration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Partnership Information Return (T5013 Summary and slips) and corresponding provincial declaration of partnership information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 5 months after the partnership fiscal year-end, with T5013 slips delivered to partners beforehand if return is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CRA late-filing penalties and interest; cumulative non-filing may generate further administrative penalties but does not by itself strike the partnership at the provincial registry

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory independent audit is mandated by Quebec law for a limited partnership; a financial review or audit is required only when the partnership agreement or a partner or creditor covenant imposes it.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: ASPE (Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises, CPA Canada Handbook Part II) for private limited partnerships; IFRS (Part I) applies if the partnership or a participating partner is a publicly accountable enterprise; partnership agreement may specify a permitted alternate framework for federal tax records.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec's legal publicity regime does not require an annual UBO declaration for limited partnerships. Any addition or removal of general or limited partners must be updated with the Registraire within the statutory change period; the internal partner register is to be maintained continuously and made available for inspection at the partnership's registered office.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners with capital contributions and contact data
Register of General Partners with identity and authority
Management Committee Minute Book and resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 340–700 per year typical Quebec corporate service provider fee
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: No statutory audit required; voluntary review or audit engagement typically USD 3,000–9,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at the Quebec limited partnership (LP) level because the LP is fiscally transparent; the combined federal and Quebec headline corporate rate applicable to the corporate general partner and corporate limited partners is 26.5% (15% federal Part I general corporate rate plus 11.5% Quebec general corporate income tax rate).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPC) and qualified Quebec SMEs may claim the Small Business Deduction, reducing the combined rate to approximately 17.0% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income (federal 9% plus Quebec 8%). Medical imaging R&D qualifies for the federal Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credit (35% refundable for CCPCs, 15% non-refundable for large corporations) and the Quebec SR&ED tax credit regime, both flowing through the LP allocation to partners. Manufacturing and processing incentives are otherwise limited; no statutory patent box applies in Quebec.
